rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hardship is constriction and difficulty; the ease is spaciousness and wealth.
rows.anchor: أي إن مع الضيقة والشدة يسرا

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: The repeated clause emphasizes and magnifies the promise, like repeated commands, repeated answers, Qur'an 102:3, and the poet's repeated appeal.
rows.anchor: وذلك للإطناب والمبالغة . قاله الفراء . ومنه قول الشاعر :

rows.speaker: ثعلب
rows.claim: In Arab usage, repeating a definite noun refers to the same thing, while repeating an indefinite noun refers to another; thus there are two eases, strengthening hope and patience.
rows.anchor: وهما اثنان ، ليكون أقوى للأمل ، وأبعث على الصبر . قاله ثعلب .

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: God created one hardship and two eases, so one hardship cannot overcome two eases.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس : يقول الله تعالى خلقت عسرا واحدا ، وخلقت يسرين ، ولن يغلب عسر يسرين

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report about this sura quotes the Prophet saying that one hardship will never overcome two eases; Qurtubi gives no grading here.
rows.anchor: وجاء في الحديث عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في هذه السورة : أنه قال : [ لن يغلب عسر يسرين ]

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masud swears that even if hardship were inside a stone, ease would pursue it and enter; one hardship cannot overcome two eases.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن مسعود{[16173]} : والذي نفسي بيده ، لو كان العسر في حجر ، لطلبه اليسر حتى يدخل عليه

rows.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
rows.claim: Replying to Abu Ubayda's concern about Roman forces, Umar assures him that a believer's hardship is followed by relief, cites this promise, and invokes 3:200.
rows.anchor: فكتب إليه عمر رضي الله عنهما : أما بعد ، فإنه مهما ينزل بعبد مؤمن من منزل شدة ، يجعل الله بعده فرجا

rows.speaker: الجرجاني
rows.claim: Al-Jurjani rejects the definite-versus-indefinite argument as unsound: its logic would make two mentions of a horse and sword imply one horse but two swords.
rows.anchor: وقال قوم منهم الجرجاني : هذا قول مدخول ؛ لأنه يجب على هذا التدريج إذا قال الرجل : إن مع الفارس سيفا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qurtubi prefers a contextual reading: the poor Prophet was mocked for poverty, became distressed, and God consoled him by promising prompt worldly relief.
rows.anchor: والصحيح أن يقال : إن الله بعث نبيه محمدا صلى الله عليه وسلم مقلا مخفا ، فعيره المشركون بفقره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The worldly promise was fulfilled before the Prophet died: he conquered the Hijaz and Yemen, gained wealth, gave lavish gifts including 200 camels, and kept a year's provisions for his family.
rows.anchor: فأنجز له ما وعده ، فلم يمت حتى فتح عليه الحجاز واليمن ، ووسع ذات يده ، حتى كان يعطي الرجل المائتين من الإبل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although the first worldly favor was specific to the Prophet, some of his community may also receive it, God willing.
rows.anchor: وإن كان خاصا بالنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ، فقد يدخل فيه بعض أمته إن شاء الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second clause begins a new promise because it has no coordinating particle such as fa or waw to mark it as joined to the first.
rows.anchor: والدليل على ابتدائه ، تعريه من فاء أو واو أو غيرها من حروف النسق التي تدل على العطف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second promise is for all believers: hardship in this world necessarily accompanies ease in the afterlife, though worldly and afterlife ease may also coincide.
rows.anchor: فهذا وعد عام لجميع المؤمنين ، لا يخرج أحد منه ، أي إن مع العسر في الدنيا للمؤمنين يسرا في الآخرة لا محالة . وربما اجتمع يسر الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report that one hardship cannot overcome two eases means worldly ease might be overcome, but afterlife ease is certain and nothing can overcome it.
rows.anchor: وإنما يغلب أحدهما إن غلب ، وهو يسر الدنيا ، فأما يسر الآخرة فكائن لا محالة ، ولن يغلبه شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation makes the hardship the Prophet's expulsion from Mecca and the ease his honorable return at its conquest with ten thousand men.
rows.anchor: وهو إخراج أهل مكة النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم من مكة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة
rows.claim: When you finish prayer, intensify supplication and ask God for what you need.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس وقتادة : فإذا فرغت من صلاتك

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: When you finish the obligatory prayers, devote yourself to standing in night prayer.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن مسعود : إذا فرغت من الفرائض فانصب في قيام الليل .

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: When you finish conveying the message, seek forgiveness for yourself and for believing men and women.
rows.anchor: وقال الكلبي : إذا فرغت من تبليغ الرسالة

rows.speaker: الحسن وقتادة
rows.claim: When you finish fighting your enemy, devote yourself to worship of your Lord.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن وقتادة أيضا : إذا فرغت من جهاد عدوك ، فانصب لعبادة ربك .

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: When you finish worldly affairs, devote yourself to prayer; a similar explanation is transmitted from al-Hasan.
rows.anchor: وعن مجاهد :  " فإذا فرغت "  من دنياك ،    " فانصب "  في صلاتك

rows.speaker: الجنيد
rows.claim: When you finish dealing with creation, strive in worship of the Real.
rows.anchor: وقال الجنيد : إذا فرغت من أمر الخلق ، فاجتهد في عبادة الحق .

rows.speaker: ابن العربي
rows.claim: Ibn al-Arabi rejects an innovator reading with kasra and initial hamza that takes the verse to mean appoint a successor-imam; it is invalid in reading and meaning, since the Prophet appointed no successor.
rows.anchor: قال ابن العربي :  " ومن المبتدعة من قرأ هذه الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some ignorant people doubled the b and read it as urging return home after jihad. Qurtubi rejects the reading as contrary to consensus, though he accepts its meaning on the basis of a travel report.
rows.anchor: فجد في الرجوع إلى بلدك

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet said travel is a piece of torment that prevents sleep, food, and drink, so after completing one's need one should hurry back to one's family; this supports the meaning of returning home.
rows.anchor: لقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم : [ السفر قطعة من العذاب ، يمنع أحدكم نومه وطعامه وشرابه ، فإذا قضى أحدكم نهمته ، فليعجل الرجوع إلى أهله ]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qurtubi condemns taking a sound meaning and attaching to it a self-invented reading or hadith, because that makes one lie about God and His Messenger.
rows.anchor: وأشد الناس عذابا وأسوأهم مباء ومآبا ، من أخذ معنى صحيحا ، فركب عليه من قبل نفسه قراءة أو حديثا ، فيكون كاذبا على الله

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر المنصور
rows.claim: Al-Mahdawi reports that Abu Ja'far al-Mansur read the opening of the sura with a fatḥa on the ḥāʾ; Qurtubi calls this far-fetched.
rows.anchor: وروي عن أبي جعفر المنصور : أنه قرأ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qurtubi offers a possible analysis of that reading: an unvoiced emphatic nūn was assumed, changed to alif at pause, carried into connected speech, then deleted; Tarafa's line illustrates the intended form اضربن.
rows.anchor: وقد يؤول على تقدير النون الخفيفة ، ثم أبدلت النون ألفا في الوقف ، ثم حمل الوصل على الوقف ، ثم حذف الألف . وأنشد عليه :

rows.speaker: أبو السمال
rows.claim: Abu al-Sammal read faraghta with kasra on the rāʾ; Qurtubi identifies it as a dialectal form.
rows.anchor: وروي عن أبي السمال  " فإذا فرغت "  بكسر الراء ، وهي لغة فيه .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A variant reads farghiba, meaning urge people to desire what is with God.
rows.anchor: أي فرغب الناس إلى ما عنده .

rows.speaker: شريح
rows.claim: Shurayh rebuked people playing on Eid, saying the lawgiver had not commanded it; Ibn al-Arabi questions this judgment.
rows.anchor: قال ابن العربي : روي عن شريح أنه مر بقوم يلعبون يوم عيد ، فقال : ما بهذا أمر الشارع . وفيه نظر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn al-Arabi counters that Abyssinians played with shields and spears in the mosque on Eid while the Prophet watched.
rows.anchor: فإن الحبش كانوا يلعبون بالدرق والحراب في المسجد يوم العيد ، والنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ينظر .

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: When Abu Bakr objected to two Ansari girls singing at Aisha's home, the Prophet told him to leave them because it was Eid.
rows.anchor: ودخل أبو بكر في بيت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم على عائشة رضي الله عنها وعندها جاريتان من جواري الأنصار تغنيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Constant, uninterrupted work is not obligatory; Qurtubi says it is disliked for human beings.
rows.anchor: وليس يلزم الدؤوب على العمل ، بل هو مكروه للخلق .

rows.speaker: يحيي بن سلام وابن عباس والجمهور
rows.claim: Yahya ibn Sallam calls the sura Meccan, while Ibn Abbas and most scholars call it Medinan; it has nine verses.
rows.anchor: وهي مكية في قول يحيي بن سلام ، ومدنية  في قول ابن عباس والجمهور . وهي تسع

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report promising immense rewards for learning this sura says people would abandon family and wealth to learn it, that angels recite it continually, and that reciters receive angelic protection and prayers; Qurtubi says the report is unsound, and Ibn al-Arabi calls its version false.
rows.anchor: قال رسول اللّه صلى اللّه

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: In the sound report from Anas, God ordered the Prophet to recite this sura to Ubayy ibn Ka'b; when Ubayy asked whether God had named him, the Prophet said yes and Ubayy wept. Bukhari and Muslim transmit it.
rows.anchor: عن أنس أن النبي صلى اللّه عليه وسلم قال لأبي بن كعب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qurtubi draws a legal lesson from the report: a teacher may recite to a learner.
rows.anchor: وفيه من الفقه قراءة العالم على المتعلم

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some say the Prophet recited to Ubayy to teach humility, so no one would disdain learning from or reading to someone lower in rank.
rows.anchor: قال بعضهم : إنما قرأ النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم على أبي ، ليعلم الناس التواضع ؛ لئلا يأنف أحد من التعلم والقراءة على من دونه في المنزلة .

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Another view says Ubayy learned the Prophet's wording especially quickly, so the Prophet recited to him for exact transmission and to enable him to teach others.
rows.anchor: وقيل : لأن أبيا كان أسرع أخذا لألفاظ رسول اللّه صلى اللّه عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: أبي بن كعب
rows.claim: A statement about Adam's greed for wealth, death filling his belly, and God's acceptance of repentance was attributed to Ubayy's reading of this sura.
rows.anchor: عن زر بن حبيش قال في قراءة أبي بن كعب : ابن آدم لو أعطي واديا من مال لالتمس ثانيا

rows.speaker: أبو بكر الأنباري
rows.claim: Abu Bakr al-Anbari says this addition is false as Qur'an: the connected readings of Ibn Kathir and Abu Amr, both traced to Ubayy, omit it; it is known as the Prophet's speech, not God's Qur'an, and consensus outweighs one contrary report.
rows.anchor: قال أبو بكر : هذا باطل عند أهل العلم ، لأن قراءتي ابن كثير وأبي عمرو متصلتان بأبي بن كعب ، لا يقرأ فيها هذا المذكور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The public reading and the consonantal text of the codex have lam yakun alladhina kafaru.
rows.anchor: قوله تعالى : { لم يكن الذين كفروا } كذا قراءة العامة ، وخط المصحف .

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masud's wording, the polytheists and People of the Book did not cease, is an explanatory reading rather than a recitation; Ibn al-Arabi allows it for exposition only, since recitation is what the codex contains.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن مسعود " لم يكن المشركون وأهل الكتاب منفكين " وهذه قراءة على التفسير .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ahl al-Kitab means Jews and Christians; al-mushrikin is genitive, coordinated with Ahl al-Kitab.
rows.anchor: قوله تعالى : { من أهل الكتاب } يعني اليهود والنصارى { والمشركين } في موضع جر عطفا على { أهل الكتاب } .

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the People of the Book as the Jews of Yathrib—Qurayza, Nadir, and Banu Qaynuqa—and the polytheists as Quraysh in Mecca and its vicinity.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس { أهل الكتاب } : اليهود الذين كانوا بيثرب ، وهم قريظة والنضير وبنو قينقاع .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Munfakkin means ceasing from disbelief or turning away from it.
rows.anchor: منتهين عن كفرهم ، مائلين عنه .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qurtubi explains the wording until the clear proof comes as until the clear proof came, referring to Muhammad.
rows.anchor: أي أتتهم البينة ، أي محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation takes infikak as reaching an endpoint: they would not reach the end of their lives and die until the clear proof came.
rows.anchor: وقيل : الانتهاء بلوغ الغاية ، أي لم يكونوا ليبلغوا نهاية أعمارهم فيموتوا ، حتى تأتيهم البينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another gloss is vanishing: their allotted time would not expire until a messenger came.
rows.anchor: أي لم تكن مدتهم لتزول حتى يأتيهم رسول .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The root f-k-k carries the sense of opening or separating; Arab idiom ما انفككت أفعل and ما انفك فلان قائما means continuing or remaining.
rows.anchor: الفك : الفتح ،   ومنه فك الكتاب ، وفك الخلخال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another gloss is departing: they would not leave and pass from the world until the clear proof came.
rows.anchor: بارحين ، أي لم يكونوا ليبرحوا ويفارقوا الدنيا ، حتى تأتيهم البينة .

rows.speaker: ابن كيسان
rows.claim: Ibn Kaysan says the People of the Book retained descriptions of Muhammad in their scriptures until his mission, then envied and denied him, as in 2:89 and 98:4.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن كيسان : أي لم يكن أهل الكتاب تاركين صفة محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم في كتابهم

rows.speaker: ابن كيسان
rows.claim: On Ibn Kaysan's reading, the Meccan polytheists called Muhammad al-Amin and did not speak ill of him until the clear proof came and they opposed him.
rows.anchor: وعلى هذا { والمشركين } أي ما كانوا يسيئون القول في محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم ، حتى بعث

rows.speaker: بعض اللغويين
rows.claim: Some linguists derive munfakkin from a woman's pelvic bone separating during childbirth and failing to reunite; the verse then means they are not punished or destroyed until messengers and books establish proof.
rows.anchor: وقال بعض اللغويين :  " منفكين "  هالكين من قولهم : انفك صلا

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: One view includes the polytheists among the People of the Book, citing Jews who called Ezra God's son and Christians who called Jesus God, His son, or one of three.
rows.anchor: وقال قوم في المشركين : إنهم من أهل الكتاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view distinguishes them by history: the People of the Book believed before disbelieving after their prophets, while polytheists began in natural disposition and disbelieved upon maturity.
rows.anchor: وقيل : أهل الكتاب كانوا مؤمنين ، ثم كفروا بعد أنبيائهم . والمشركون ولدوا على الفطرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view takes polytheists as a description of the People of the Book too: they abandoned monotheism and their scriptures, since Christians are trinitarian and most Jews anthropomorphists; all are shirk.
rows.anchor: وقيل : المشركون وصف أهل الكتاب أيضا ، لأنهم لم ينتفعوا بكتابهم ، وتركوا التوحيد .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation restricts disbelief to rejection of Muhammad: the People of the Book are Jews and Christians, while the polytheists are idol worshippers without scripture.
rows.anchor: وقيل : إن الكفر هنا هو الكفر بالنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ، أي لم يكن الذين كفروا بمحمد

rows.speaker: القشيري
rows.claim: Al-Qushayri finds that interpretation strained because the following phrase identifies the clear proof as Muhammad; it can work only if it means they persisted in present disbelief until Muhammad came, explained the signs, and some then believed.
rows.anchor: قال القشيري : وفيه بعد ؛ لأن الظاهر من { حتى تأتيهم البينة . رسول من الله } أن هذا الرسول هو محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: الأعمش وإبراهيم
rows.claim: Al-A'mash and Ibrahim read al-mushrikun in the nominative, coordinated with alladhina; Qurtubi prefers the genitive reading because nominative makes both groups seem outside the People of the Book.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الأعمش وإبراهيم " والمشركون " رفعا ، عطفا على

rows.speaker: أبي بن كعب
rows.claim: Ubayy's codex has the variant فما كان الذين كفروا من أهل الكتاب والمشركون منفكين.
rows.anchor: وفي حرف أبيّ : " فما كان الذين كفروا من أهل الكتاب والمشركون منفكين "

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rasul means an emissary sent by God.
rows.anchor: أي بعيث من الله جل ثناؤه .

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj parses rasul as nominative in apposition to al-bayyina.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج : { رسول } رفع على البدل من  " البينة " .

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra reads the construction as either it is a messenger from God or he is a messenger from God, since bayyina can be spoken of as a person.
rows.anchor: وقال الفراء : أي هي رسول من الله ، أو هو رسول من الله ؛ لأن البينة قد تذكر

rows.speaker: أبي وابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ubayy and Ibn Masud have rasulan in the accusative, as an independent or specification accusative.
rows.anchor: وفي حرف أبي وابن مسعود { رسولا } بالنصب على القطع .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yatlu means to read or recite.
rows.anchor: { يتلو } أي يقرأ . يقال : تلا يتلو تلاوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Suhuf is the plural of sahifa, the vessel or surface that holds writing.
rows.anchor: { صحفا } جمع صحيفة ، وهي ظرف المكتوب .

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة وغيرهما
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the sheets are cleared of falsehood, doubt, hypocrisy, and error; Qatada says falsehood, and others add lies, ambiguities, and disbelief—the sense is the same.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس : من الزور ، والشك ، والنفاق ، والضلالة . وقال قتادة : من الباطل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet recites the writing contained in the sheets from memory rather than from a physical book, since he was unlettered and neither wrote nor read.
rows.anchor: أي يقرأ ما تتضمن الصحف من المكتوب ؛ ويدل عليه أنه كان يتلو عن ظهر قلبه ، لا عن كتاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Though mutahhara grammatically modifies suhuf, it describes the Qur'an within them; compare the honored, elevated, purified sheets in 80:13–14.
rows.anchor: و{ مطهرة } : من نعت الصحف ، وهو كقوله تعالى : { في صحف مكرمة . مرفوعة مطهرة }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view understands the sheets to be such that none should touch them except the purified, as discussed under 56:79.
rows.anchor: أي ينبغي ألا يمسها إلا المطهرون ، كما قال في سورة

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: One view identifies the purified sheets as the heavenly original in Umm al-Kitab from which the revealed books were copied; al-Hasan says these sheets are in heaven, as in 85:21–22.
rows.anchor: قال الحسن : يعني الصحف المطهرة في السماء .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qayyima means upright, straight, sound, and firm, from the Arab root q-w-m for becoming upright and sound.
rows.anchor: أي مستقيمة مستوية محكمة ، من قول العرب : قام يقوم إذا استوى وصح .

rows.speaker: بعض أهل العلم
rows.claim: Some ask how scrolls can contain books if the scrolls are themselves books; Qurtubi answers that kutub here means rulings, as in 58:21 where the phrase means God has decreed.
rows.anchor: وقال بعض أهل العلم : الصحف هي الكتب ، فكيف قال في صحف فيها كتب ؟ فالجواب : أن الكتب هنا بمعنى الأحكام

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet's promise to judge by God's Book while ordering stoning shows that Book of God can mean God's ruling, although stoning is not written in the text.
rows.anchor: وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( والله لأقضين بينكما بكتاب الله ) ثم قضى بالرجم ، وليس ذكر الرجم مسطورا في الكتاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qurtubi uses a poetic line about what God writes to support the sense of kutub as divine decrees or rulings.
rows.anchor: وما ذاك قال اللّه إذ هو يكتب

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Another view identifies the upright books as the Qur'an, called books because it contains many kinds of exposition.
rows.anchor: وقيل : الكتب القيمة هي القرآن ، فجعله كتبا لأنه يشتمل على أنواع من البيان .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God made the People of the Elephant like crop leaves eaten by animals and spat out below; their broken limbs resembled the scattered pieces of fodder.
rows.anchor: أي جعل الله أصحاب الفيل كورق الزرع إذا أكلته الدواب ، فرمت به من أسفل . شبه تقطع أوصالهم بتفرق أجزائه .

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd and others are reported to have transmitted this explanation of the verse.
rows.anchor: روى معناه عن ابن زيد وغيره

rows.speaker: علقمة
rows.claim: Alqama's verse uses asifa for the foliage gathered around the grain head, supporting the sense of asf as crop leaves.
rows.anchor: ومما يدل على أنه ورق الزرع قول علقمة : تسقي مذانب قد مالت عصيفتها

rows.speaker: رؤبة بن العجاج
rows.claim: Ru'ba's poem recounts the Elephant army struck by stones and flocks of birds, ending by saying they became like eaten chaff.
rows.anchor:
وقال رؤبة بن العجاج :
ومسهم ما مس أصحاب الفيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Asf is a collective noun whose singular forms include asfa, asafa, and asifa.
rows.anchor: العصف : جمع ، واحدته عصفة وعصافة ، وعصيفة .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The kaf is used for comparison alongside mithl, as in 42:11, where nothing is like Him.
rows.anchor: للتشبيه مع مثل ، نحو قوله تعالى : { ليس كمثله شيء }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ma'kul means that its grain was eaten, just as calling someone handsome means that his face is handsome.
rows.anchor: كقشر الحنطة إذا خرجت منه الحبة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the comparison is to wheat chaff: the husk surrounding the wheat kernel.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس : { فجعلهم كعصف مأكول } أن المراد به قشر البر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says a stone would strike a man and bring out everything inside him, leaving him like wheat husk after the kernel is removed.
rows.anchor: ويروى أن الحجر كان يقع على أحدهم فيخرج كل ما في جوفه ، فيبقى كقشر الحنطة

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masud says God sent wind to strike the birds' stones and strengthen them, so everyone struck died; only one man from Kinda survived.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن مسعود : لما رمت الطير بالحجارة ، بعث الله ريحا فضربت الحجارة فزادتها شدة

rows.speaker: رجل من كندة
rows.claim: The surviving man from Kinda's poem recalls the birds, a passing cloud, and the disaster that befell the army at al-Mughammas.
rows.anchor: خشيت الله إذ قد بث طيرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another report says the birds did not strike all the army, only those God willed; Qurtubi leaves the matter to God.
rows.anchor: ويروى أنها لم تصبهم كلهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qurtubi adds that the commander and a small remnant returned, then died after telling others what they had seen.
rows.anchor: وقد تقدم أن أميرهم رجع وشرذمة لطيفة معه

rows.speaker: ابن إسحاق
rows.claim: Ibn Ishaq says God's repelling the Abyssinians made Arabs honor Quraysh as God's people, believing God had fought for them and spared them the enemy; this was a divine favor.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن إسحاق : لما رد الله الحبشة عن مكة ، عظمت العرب قريشا وقالوا : أهل الله ، قاتل عنهم
